summary: "As the saying goes, 'A child's character at three shows the adult at seven.' A person's character begins to take shape in infancy. If we want to help children develop good habits and character, the period before age six is absolutely critical. This book focuses on the development of children's character and habits across different age stages from 0 to 6 years old. It aligns with children's sensitive developmental periods and transforms the core principles of Montessori education into practical guides—highlighting key developmental milestones and offering simple, hands-on parent-child training games. The book presents a comprehensive, progressive, and highly practical educational plan tailored to each stage. Habits form character, and character shapes destiny. During this crucial 0–6 age window, we can work together to ensure children grow up in a nurturing family environment—where they can discover a whole, healthy sense of self

title: WHAT IF… : A Lifetime of Questions, Speculations, Reasonable Guesses, and A Few Things I Know for Sure
author: MacLaine, Shirley, 1934-
summary: "Beloved actress and bestselling author Shirley MacLaine contemplates a wealth of subjects from the mundane to the esoteric in this all-new collection of musings that begin with two simple words: What if--What if hope is the most dangerous emotion? What if a frog had wings? (Answer: He wouldnt bump his ass so much.) What if our political leaders actually led? What if Downton Abbey was full of Americans? What if, for some reason, I couldn't be creative and work? These are just a few of the what ifs that Shirley Maclaine considers in her new book written in the style of her beloved and laugh-out-loud memoir In Over All That. In What If, she speculates on a wide range of matters both spiritual and secular, humorous and profound, earth-bound and high-flying, personal and universal. This is Shirley MacLaine at her most funny, acerbic, imaginative, and irresistible."
